newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech ministers say energy deregulated by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Czech ministers say energy deregulated by 2000.

text.p: The Czech council of economic ministers on Tuesday agreed that energy prices should be fully deregulated to reflect costs by the year 2000, Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl told journalists.
"By 2000, the prices (of energy) should cover costs," Kuhnl said, meaning artificial price controls would be fully removed.
Meanwhile, Kuhnl told Reuters that the distribution network of the largest Czech power producer CEZ a.s. should be divested by the year 2000 to create more competition.
CEZ, in which the government still holds a two-thirds stake, is the largest power producer and controls much of the country's electricity distribution.
The government has been looking for ways to create more competition in the power industry.
Both decisions require the approval of the full cabinet.
Further details on how the seperation of CEZ's distribution network would take place have not been announced.
The question of energy deregulation has been one of the most fiercely fought issues within the centre-right government, and has brought the three-party ruling coalition to the verge of collapse.
The two right-wing party's in the coalition, including Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's senior Civic Democratic Party, have insisted on faster deregulation of energy and controlled housing prices.

The centrist junior Christian Democrats have pushed to have deregulation delayed, especially as government austerity measures of budget cuts and wage freezes, announced in April and May to address serious macroecnomic problems, are carried out.
